svg.text: LP-MSPM0G3507, seen from above, USB unplugged. Add the wires in the numbered order; each number sits at both ends of its wire and in the list below. The schematic shows the same circuit in symbols.
J1 and J2 are the outer columns, J3 and J4 the inner ones; pin 1, 21, 40 and 20 are at the USB end.
Wire colours: red 3.3 V, orange 5 V, black ground; every other colour is one signal.

g.text: Breadboard: holes a to e, and f to j, in one column are joined; each long rail is joined end to end.
Column 1 is at this end; rails and holes count up toward the top.
Wires, in the order you add them
Place first: Breadboard power module, WS2812B LED strip
Bottom ground rail, hole 25 to J3 pin 22 (GND)
Strip 5 V to Bottom 5 V rail, hole 22
Strip GND to Bottom ground rail, hole 22
WS2812 LED ring: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
Breadboard power module: + pin in bp1, − pin in bm1
WS2812B LED strip: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
The ring's data pin wants a 5 V signal; at 3.3 V most rings work, but keep the data wire short.
The breadboard power module takes 6.5 to 12 V on its barrel jack or 5 V on its USB; set both jumpers to 5 V; its ground must join the LaunchPad ground.

A 60-LED strip at full white draws up to 3.6 A, more than a breadboard power module or its rails can carry: keep the program's brightness low (it caps the strip), or feed the strip's 5 V and ground from a 5 V 4 A adapter straight to its pads, ground shared with the LaunchPad. Take the ring's wires off before the strip's.
Then plug in USB, run the build, and expect
The rainbow runs along the strip. If only the first few LEDs light, check the ground tie.
The same circuit as a schematic

svg.text: Fox Red Labs. Pins from the build's pin table, the one the program is built from; the 3D build on the page shows the same wiring step by step. Board picture: TI SLAU873E, figure 1-1.
